title: Ion Drive Dungeon Power Core Simulation
description: The user operates a dungeon power facility where an ancient warkarma dungeon structure houses a futuristic ion drive as its central energy core. The player must calibrate the ion drive through a multi-step startup sequence—adjusting thrust output, plasma frequency, containment field strength, and cooling flow—while monitoring the dungeon structure for structural integrity warnings as energy levels rise.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive dungeon power core simulation. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader: place dungeon_warkarma.glb as the environment structure centered at the origin scaled appropriately, and place PrimaryIonDrive.glb inside the dungeon as the central power core, floating slightly above the dungeon floor with a slow idle rotation. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 4, 8) looking at the origin. Add ambient light (intensity 0.3), a blue-tinted point light near the ion drive, and a dim orange directional light for dungeon atmosphere. Use OrbitControls with constrained vertical angle. Create an HTML overlay panel with these interactive controls: (1) a Start Ignition button that begins the sequence, (2) a thrust output slider (0-100%) that must be set between 60-80% for safe operation, (3) a plasma frequency slider (1-10 Hz) requiring value 4-6 Hz, (4) a containment field strength slider (0-100%) requiring 75-95%, (5) a coolant flow toggle that must be enabled, and (6) a final Engage Full Power button that validates all parameters. When ignition starts, make the ion drive glow by adding an emissive material override that pulses. As thrust increases, increase the ion drive rotation speed and point light intensity proportionally. If any parameter is out of safe range when Engage is pressed, flash the dungeon model red and display a warning. When all parameters are valid and Engage is pressed, trigger a success state: the ion drive emits expanding ring particle effects using a BufferGeometry ring of points, the dungeon interior lights shift to bright blue-white, and a status display shows CORE ONLINE. Track and display a stability percentage that fluctuates based on parameter accuracy. All sliders must update the simulation in real-time with visible feedback.
